Bug_Title: MC: An overridable method is called from the clone() method. (MC_OVERRIDABLE_METHOD_CALL_IN_CLONE)
Bug_Details:
Calling overridable methods from the clone() method is insecure because a subclass could override the method,
affecting the behavior of clone(). It can also observe or modify the clone object in a partially initialized
state. Only static, final or private methods should be invoked from the clone() method. 
See SEI CERT rule
MET06-J. Do not invoke overridable methods in clone().
Bug_Explanation: An overridable method mutateData is called from the overridden clone() method. This is dangerous because the subclass might override the method, causing unpredictable behavior.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the mutateData method is called from the clone method, which is overridden in the test case. The mutateData method changes the state of the clone object, but this change is not preserved in the clone object because the clone method does not handle state cloning correctly.
